The story is told strictly from the third-person limited perspective of a single character, Barbara Rosen. It does not offer diverse perspectives or dive into the mindsets of other characters. Most notably, the young man who commits the murder—whose actions are certainly objectionable and repugnant—is viewed entirely from the outside. The reader is never given access to his internal viewpoint, beliefs, or motivations; his actions are explicitly left as "incomprehensible," and he remains an external, unreadable figure to the protagonist.
